# Datasheet — FinSight Synthetic Transaction Ledger

*A Gebru-style datasheet for the synthetic dataset generated by
`generate_data.py` / `finance_agent/datagen.py`. This document answers the
standard datasheet questions truthfully — including the parts that are
limitations. The companion machine-readable benchmark record lives in
[`model_bench/best_model_metadata.json`](../model_bench/best_model_metadata.json)
and the auto-generated model card in [`model_bench/MODEL_CARD.md`](../model_bench/MODEL_CARD.md).

---

## Motivation

**For what purpose was the dataset created?** To power an end-to-end demo of
explainable, agentic personal-finance fraud detection: deterministic synthetic
ledgers with *labeled* injected fraud, so evaluation is meaningful, reproducible,
and free of privacy/licensing concerns. The labels exist to answer *"did the
model catch the fraud?"* per archetype — not to train a production model.

**Who created it?** The FinSight Agent project (synthetic data is a design
choice, not a proxy for scraped data). There is no collection event behind this
dataset.

## Composition

**What is in the dataset?** One row per transaction. Columns are the PaySim-style
legacy set (`step`, `type`, `amount`, `nameOrig`, `nameDest`, `oldbalanceOrg`,
`newbalanceOrig`, `oldbalanceDest`, `newbalanceDest`, `merchant`, `category`,
`datetime`, `date`, `is_focal_user`, `isFraud`, `isFlaggedFraud`, `is_anomaly`,
`anomaly_type`) plus the v2 persona columns (`persona_id`, `persona_archetype`,
`account_type`, `merchant_region`, `transaction_region`, `home_region`,
`category_group`, `subcategory`, `fraud_archetype`, `label_reported_at_step`,
`simulation_year`). See `docs/technical/Schema.md §2`.

**How many instances?** Tier-dependent: `tiny` ≈ 20 background accounts,
`demo` ≈ 2,000 background + 1 focal user over 90 days, `bench` ≈ 20,000
background + 200 focal personas over 4 years (10M+ rows, Parquet).

**Does the dataset contain all possible instances?** No. It is a finite
simulation window per tier; the generator is parameterizable (`--days`,
`--seed`, `--n-background-accounts`, `--focal-users`, `--start-date`).

**What data does each instance consist of?** Raw transaction attributes plus
engineered, strictly backward-looking features (`finance_agent/features.py`),
and a `fraud_archetype` label for injected fraud (empty for legitimate rows).

**Composition by archetype.** Six persona archetypes
(`young_professional`, `dual_income_family`, `gig_worker`, `retiree`,
`recent_graduate`, `small_business_owner`). Every persona is drawn from its
archetype prior with its own seeded RNG substream, so individuals differ
within an archetype. Fraud is injected from a 15-pattern library graded by
difficulty:

| Tier | Patterns (fraud_archetype) | Difficulty |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Easy (rule-detectable) | `balance_drain`, `duplicate_charge`, `spend_spike` | easy |
| Medium (needs the model) | `card_testing`, `slow_balance_drain`, `new_payee_transfer`, `subscription_creep`, `refund_abuse` | medium |
| Hard / adversarial | `mimicry`, `account_takeover`, `bust_out` (background), `seasonal_mimicry` | hard |
| Hard negatives (NOT fraud) | `life_event`, `travel`, `rapid_burst` | — |

Fraud rate is configurable per tier (`fraud_scale`, `bust_fraction`) and lands
in a defensible real-world-adjacent band (≈0.1–1%).

**Is any information missing?** Deliberately: no free-text narratives, no
geo-precise locations (only coarse region ids like `R00_portland`), no
personally identifying details. `fraud_archetype` is empty for non-fraud rows
by design.

**Are there duplicate instances?** No — every row is a distinct generated
event. `duplicate_charge` *simulates* a duplicate charge as a labeled anomaly,
but the rows themselves are unique.

## Collection process

**How was the data acquired?** It was generated, not collected:
1. A top-level seed derives per-persona `SeedSequence` substreams
   (reproducibility contract: reordering one persona's generation can never
   perturb another's data).
2. Each persona's income cadence (weekly/biweekly/semimonthly/monthly/
   irregular), rent, savings rate, category weights, subscriptions, raises,
   and travel regions are sampled from archetype priors.
3. Transaction streams are drawn with vectorized NumPy operations (Poisson
   draws per category per day, lognormal amounts), then balances are applied
   with a per-account clamped cumulative sum (Lindley recursion).
4. Fraud/anomaly patterns inject labeled rows with discovery lag
   (`label_reported_at_step` may be later than `step`, mimicking
   chargeback-reporting delay).

**Who was involved?** The generation codebase; no human subjects, no external
vendors, no crowdsourcing.

**Over what timeframe?** The simulation window — 90 days for tiny/demo, 4
years for bench. "Time" is simulated via hourly `step` counters.

**Does the dataset relate to people?** Only synthetic personas. No real
individuals, no real PII, no real accounts.

## Preprocessing / cleaning

- Balance-dependent fraud amounts (drains) are resolved in a second pass so
  balances always chain correctly (enforced by `tests/test_generate_data.py`).
- The final frame is column-ordered to the canonical `FINAL_COLUMNS` and
  amount is cast to float.
- Feature engineering (`finance_agent/features.py`) is applied at training and
  inference time, strictly backward-looking to avoid temporal leakage
  (enforced by `tests/test_features.py::test_no_temporal_leakage`).
- The bench tier is stored as Parquet with arrow-backed strings to keep memory
  practical at 10M+ rows.

## Uses

**What has the dataset been used for?** (a) benchmarking six fraud-detection
models with temporal split + 5-fold time-series CV; (b) the Streamlit demo app
(dashboard, risk scan, reports); (c) the agent's facts tools and LLM grounding
tests. All within this repository.

**Is there anything the dataset should not be used for?** Anything involving
real money, real accounts, real people, or production decisions. The dataset is
a synthetic demo artifact — its fraud patterns are deliberately
rule-detectable and its absolute metrics are illustrative of *method*, not of
real-world fraud rates. See `docs/KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md`.

## Distribution

**How is the dataset distributed?** Generated on demand (`make data`,
`make data-tiny`, `make data-bench`) from the committed generator — the raw
CSV/Parquet is not distributed. The canonical benchmark record that *is*
committed is `model_bench/best_model_metadata.json` (mean ± std CV metrics,
per-archetype recall, cohort fairness, calibration) and the auto-generated
`model_bench/MODEL_CARD.md`.

**When was it released / licensed?** MIT, part of the FinSight Agent project.

## Maintenance

**Who maintains the dataset?** The repository maintainers. The generator is
versioned in git; a `seed` counter (`model_bench/SEED_COUNTER`) and the weekly
retrain workflow regenerate the ledger reproducibly.

## Known limitations (honest section)

- **Synthetic distributions, not real data.** Income/spend/fraud distributions
  are modeled priors, not measured reality. Absolute numbers (fraud rates,
  PR-AUC) are method illustrations.
- **Hard-tier recall is deliberately imperfect.** `mimicry`,
  `account_takeover`, and `seasonal_mimicry` are designed so a good model still
  misses some — the honest per-archetype table is the point.
- **No temporal novelty.** Seasonality, raises, and drift exist, but real-world
  regime changes (new product lines, policy changes) do not.
- **Label noise is simulated, not real.** Discovery lag is injected at ~2%,
  which approximates — but does not reproduce — real fraud-reporting delay.
